extracted.intended_audience: journalism scholars, media studies students, and reporters interested in news production
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the criteria and concepts used to evaluate and produce news (selection, verification, formats, institutional practices) as presented in a scholarly book on newsmaking. Useful for analyzing newsrooms, newsworthiness, and news film conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The process and standards by which reporters substantiate factual claims (listed under 'Verification of facts', pp. 83-86).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced alongside 'Substantiation'; detailed discussion appears in the indicated pages. Implies procedures and norms for checking facts before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources: access to media
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to media by sources and how centralized sources affect news (entries: access to media and, centralized, institutionalized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes issues of institutionalized sources, centralized access, and the outlook/position of sources (see pages 18-23, 81, 94n, 210, 214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and facts as mutually determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: The mutual determinacy of sources and the facts they supply—how source selection shapes what counts as fact and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index cross-references (81, 84, 90, 213) indicate a theoretical treatment; relates to practices like imputing facts, legitimating facts, and relocating facticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts and quotation marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of quotation and attributions in treating material as factual (entry: facts and, quotation marks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to how reporters' use of quotes/attribution supports or distances the reporter from factual claims (see pp. 95-97).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hoarding of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of 'hoarding' sources—cultivating privileged access—which affects story selection and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed as 'hoarding' (pp. 73-74, 78-79); implies an organizational strategy and an ethical/practical implication for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proven reliability of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating sources by their proven reliability as a basis for publishing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed under sources (p. 93); connects to verification and institutionalized judgments about credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocating facticity / Web of facticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices that move or reconstitute what counts as fact (the 'web of facticity' and relocating facticity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in relation to sources, quotes, and news film (see pp. 90-92, 107, 109-11, 123-24). Signals that 'facts' are constructed within news practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Timeliness"
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness as a central criterion of newsworthiness (indexed as '*Timeliness,*' and tied to spot and developing news).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to typifications, spot news, deadlines, tempo and what-a-story (see pp. 39-47, 51-56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of typifications (news categories and routines) to reduce variability and organize incoming events into newsworthy forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes typifications as objectified, consequences of typifications, continuing news, developing news, hard news, soft news, spot news, and what-a-story (pp. 46-63, 65, 211-12, 215).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft news (feature stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature/soft news as a mode and typification distinct from hard news (entries: Soft news, mode of presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers presentation conventions and placement; noted differences on television and as typification (pp. 47-48, 98, 100-101, 131-32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot news / Developing news
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of unscheduled, rapidly unfolding events (spot news) and the routines for developing such stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed under Spot news and Developing news (pp. 47-50, 51-56, 102-103). Tied to timeliness and typifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard news
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard news as a typified category distinct from soft news, with its own production routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in relation to typifications and workflows (pp. 51-53, 56-58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Story forms / Narrative forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal story/narrative structures used in news (listed as 'Story (-ies): forms' and 'Narrative forms').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the idea that news is presented as story; see pp. 100-103 and references to storytelling conventions and paper writing (pp. 105, 187, 217).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling as a mode of news
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of storytelling conventions to produce news (storytelling as mode of news; storytelling conventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects selection and presentation practices; connects to work flow and typifications (pp. 105, 217).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value judgments: distinction between facts and value judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a distinction between factual reporting and evaluative/value judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed under 'Value judgments' (pp. 99-100); implies editorial norms about separating description from evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and truth-claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptions of truth in news: ideological vs. scientific truth and the handling of truth-claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as 'Truth' and 'Truth-claims' (pp. 100, 165-78, 90-92, 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work (work flow) control
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization and control of newsroom work flow, including prediction, allocation, and routines for hard vs soft news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers control of work, allocation of reporters, prediction-driven workflows, and connections to typifications and storytelling (pp. 44, 46-58, 65, 74, 107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal organization: tempo, scheduling, deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: How time is organized in news production—tempo, scheduling, temporal concentration/synchronization of reporters, deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include Tempo; Time; Time measurement; Temporal concentration/synchronization; Weekend scheduling; Timing of shows (pp. 39-47, 41-45, 98, 144-46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial organization: space and spatial anchoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitution of news in space, spatial anchoring of news networks, and the intertwining of space and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes public space, space in news film, and spatialized time (pp. 23-31, 109-15, 116-20, 39-41, 210).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization: organizational and topical
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of labor by organizational specialization and topical specialists in newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers specialization's effect on allocation and coverage (pp. 27-30, 29-35, 97, 101, 211).

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial editors and territoriality
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic/territorial organization of editorial responsibility (territorial editors, territoriality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates structural newsroom roles and their influence on what gets covered (pp. 30-33, 35, 150, 151, 211).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire services and centralized sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of wire services and centralized news sources in shaping coverage and facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include Associated Press, United Press International, wire-service editor and wire services (pp. 20-24, 32, 37, 159).

rubrics_metrics.name: Television news conventions and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Television-specific production criteria: news film conventions, standard shots, visual language, talking heads, budgets, licensing, Fairness Doctrine, advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers news film use of space/time, visual rendition of facticity, standard shots, talking distance, visual variation, networks' licensing and First Amendment issues, and resource allocation (pp. 107-132, 170-176, 120-24, 129-31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of reporters / systematic location of reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: How reporters are allocated in time and space (systematic location, allocation, temporal concentration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes working hours, temporal synchronization, and placement of reporters in beats and locations (pp. 18-19, 41-45, 42, 50, 54).

rubrics_metrics.name: What-a-story / unscheduled events-as-news
rubrics_metrics.description: The category 'what-a-story' for events that unexpectedly fit news criteria and the treatment of unscheduled events as news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to typifications, spot news, and selection processes for surprising occurrences (pp. 59-63, 51-53, 56, 103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock of knowledge at hand (reporters')
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters' existing stock of knowledge and how it informs coverage decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed as 'Stock of knowledge at hand, reporters’' (pp. 57-59); suggests that reporters' prior knowledge shapes what is noticed and how events are interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of stereotyping in news production and its effects on coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed simply as 'Stereotyping' (p. 188); implies an evaluative concern about biased framing and recurring patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation and attribution practices for legitimating facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of attribution, quotation marks, and sourcing practices to legitimate or distance the newsroom from factual claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to 'facts and, quotation marks', 'facts and, legitimated', and 'facts and, imputing' (pp. 91-97, 93-95).
